q: 1. The difference in placing the end of a beam simply over a support and the supporting end through a hinge on rollers is that the roller support
options: can offer reaction in the plane of rollers
will not allow the end to lift up due to deflection
will not offer reaction normal to the plane of rollers.
explain: A roller support provides a reaction only in the direction perpendicular to the plane of the rollers.

q: 2. The minimum moment of resistance of a beam with material of allowable stress σ, is given by
options: (σ * I) / Distance of farthest fibre from neutral axis
(σ * I) / distance of nearer extreme fibre
σ * I * ratio of distances of the two extreme fibres
explain: Moment of Resistance M = σ * Z. Since Z = I / y_max (farthest fiber), the formula is (σ * I) / y_max.

q: 3. Polar moment of inertia of a circular section with radius R is ............
explain: For a circle, $J = \frac{\pi D^4}{32}$. Since $D=2R$, $J = \frac{\pi (2R)^4}{32} = \frac{16\pi R^4}{32} = \frac{\pi R^4}{2}$.

q: 4. Polar moment of inertia of a hollow circular section with external diameter D and internal diameter d is ............
explain: The polar moment of inertia ($J$) for a hollow section is the difference between the $J$ of the outer circle and the $J$ of the inner circle: $\frac{\pi D^4}{32} - \frac{\pi d^4}{32}$.

q: 5. A plane section before twisting will remain plane after twisting if the cross-section is ............
explain: This is a primary assumption in the theory of pure torsion for circular shafts. Non-circular sections experience 'warping'.

q: 6. The radius of gyration of a rectangular section is not proportional to ............
options: square root of the moment of inertia
square root of the inverse of the area
square root of the moment of inertial divided by area of the section
explain: Radius of gyration k = √(I/A). It is directly proportional to √I and proportional to 1/√A. Therefore, it is proportional to √(I/A). Option (d) is chosen as the others describe its components.

q: 7. A reinforced concrete beam is assumed to be made of ............
explain: RCC is a heterogeneous material because it consists of two distinct materials (concrete and steel) acting together.

q: 8. If a constant section beam is subjected to a uniform bending moment throughout, its length bends to ............
explain: Pure bending (constant M) implies a constant curvature (1/R = M/EI). A curve with constant curvature is a circular arc.

q: 9. The product of the tangential force acting on the shaft and its distance from the axis of the shaft (i.e., radius of shaft) is known as ............
explain: Moment = Force × Distance. When the force is tangential and the distance is the radius, it causes the shaft to twist, hence it is a twisting moment or torque.

q: 10. The torsional rigidity of a shaft is given by ............
explain: Torsional rigidity is defined as the torque required to produce a unit radian of twist per unit length. From T/J = Gθ/L, GJ = TL/θ. Often represented as T/θ for a given length.

q: 11. The section modulus of a rectangular section is proportional to
options: square of the area of the section
half moment of inertia of the section
explain: Z = bd²/6 for a rectangular section — it scales with the section's area and depth together.

q: 12. Find the maximum BM induced in a cantilever beam subjected to a point load of 10 KN. Length of beam is 10 m. The load is located at a distance of 3 m from the free end:-
explain: Distance from the fixed end = 10 − 3 = 7 m. M = 10 × 7 = 70 kN-m.

q: 13. Find the maximum SF induced in a cantilever beam subjected to a point load of 10 KN. Length of beam is 10 m. The load is located at a distance of 3 m from the free end
explain: For a single point load on a cantilever, the shear force between the fixed end and the load point equals the load itself, 10 kN.

q: 14. The reaction at end A of the beam shown (UDL of 2 kN/m over a beam with overhangs of l/2 on each side of a central support arrangement) is
explain: Based on the symmetric overhang/support arrangement shown in the figure, the reaction at A works out to zero.

q: 15. Find the bending moment at center and also find the maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam of span 5 m with a 10 KN point load located 2 m from one support and 3 m from the other
explain: RA = 10×3/5 = 6 kN. BM at load point (max) = 6×2 = 12 kN-m. BM at center (2.5 m from A) = 6×2.5 − 10×0.5 = 10 kN-m.

q: 16. A cantilever beam of span 4 m and carrying a point load of 10 KN located at 3 m from the fixed end. Find the BM at the fixed and free end
explain: BM at fixed end = 10×3 = 30 kN-m; BM at the free end of any cantilever is always zero.

q: 17. The maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam is where the UDL is applied
explain: Under a full-span UDL, maximum BM occurs at mid-span.

q: 18. The maximum BM produced in a simply supported beam having span 4 m and subjected to a UDL of 10 kN/m
explain: M_max = wL²/8 = 10×4²/8 = 20 kN-m.

q: 19. The maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam loaded with a UDL of w/m having span l is
explain: Standard formula: M_max = wl²/8 for a full-span UDL on a simply supported beam.

q: 20. Maximum bending moment occurs at the centre if the simply supported beam is subjected to
options: uniformly distributed load throughout the span
triangular load with maximum intensity at centre
explain: All three symmetric loading patterns produce maximum BM at mid-span for a simply supported beam.

q: 21. Find the maximum SF induced in a S.S beam if the beam is subjected to a point load of 4 KN at the centre of beam and span of the beam is 4 m
explain: Each support reaction = W/2 = 4/2 = 2 kN, which is the maximum shear force.

q: 22. If y is the deflection of the beam, then shear force is
explain: V = EI·d³y/dx³ — shear force is the third derivative of deflection (times EI).

q: 23. The relation between deflection (y) and bending moment (M) is
explain: The Euler-Bernoulli beam equation: M = -EI·d²y/dx² (sign convention dependent).

q: 24. The relation between the radius of curvature (R), bending moment (M) and flexural rigidity (EI) is given by
explain: From the bending equation: M/I = E/R, so M = EI/R.

q: 25. Along the neutral axis of a simply supported beam
options: the fibres are subjected to maximum stress
explain: By definition, the neutral axis is the locus of zero bending stress/strain.

q: 26. Simple bending equation is
explain: The standard bending equation: M/I = f/y = E/R.

q: 27. Maximum bending moment occurs where
options: shear force is less than one
explain: Since V=dM/dx, M is at an extremum (max/min) where V=0, i.e. where the shear force diagram crosses zero and changes sign.

q: 28. In a beam where shear force is maximum the bending moment will be
explain: As per the answer key; there's no fixed universal relation between the location of max SF and the BM value there — it depends on the specific loading case.

q: 29. Shape of bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam having point load at centre is
explain: BM varies linearly from zero at supports to maximum under the point load — forming a triangle.

q: 30. Bending moment diagram of simply supported beam having uniformly distributed load is
explain: BM under UDL varies as a second-degree curve (parabola), zero at supports, maximum at mid-span.

q: 31. The variation of the bending moment in the portion of the beam carrying linearly varying load is
explain: A linearly varying load (triangular) produces a shear force that's parabolic and a bending moment that's cubic in x.

q: 32. The variation of the bending moment in the segment of a beam where the load is uniformly distributed is
explain: Under UDL, shear varies linearly and bending moment (its integral) varies parabolically.

q: 33. The bending moment diagram for a cantilever beam subjected to a moment at the end of the beam would be
explain: A pure end moment with no other loads produces a constant BM throughout — a rectangle.

q: 34. A beam simply supported at ends is subjected to load. The maximum bending moment is located where
explain: Since dM/dx = V, BM is maximum/minimum exactly where V = 0.

q: 35. Point of contraflexure is a point where bending moment
explain: At a point of contraflexure the bending moment passes through zero, changing from sagging to hogging (or vice versa).

q: 36. In a continuous beam, the point where bending moment changes sign is called
explain: All three terms describe the same location where BM sign reverses.

q: 37. The point of contraflexure occurs in a beam
explain: Contraflexure points typically arise in overhanging beams (and continuous beams), where sagging and hogging regions meet.

q: 38. In a fixed beam, the points of contraflexure,
options: for a moment applied load are 2
explain: Fixed beams develop two points of contraflexure for each of these standard load cases.

q: 39. In case of a fixed beam loaded at its centre, the number of points at which BM is zero
explain: A centrally-loaded fixed beam has two points of contraflexure (zero BM), symmetric about mid-span.

q: 40. The maximum bending moment caused by a moving load on a simply supported beam is
explain: For a single moving point load, the maximum BM occurs directly under the load at its critical position.

q: 41. The maximum bending moment caused by a moving load on a fixed end beam occurs
explain: For a fixed-end beam, the largest bending moment from a moving load typically develops at the supports (fixed ends).

q: 42. If a cantilever beam carries a uniformly distributed load over its entire length, then the shape of the shear force diagram and bending moment diagram respectively are
explain: Under UDL, SF is linear (triangle) and BM is a second-degree (quadratic) parabola.

q: 43. The variation of the bending moment in the segment of a beam where no external load is present is
explain: With zero load, shear force is constant, so BM (its integral) varies linearly.

q: 44. The critical bending moment caused in a fixed end beam loaded with a uniformly distributed load (W=wL) throughout is
explain: For a fixed-fixed beam under UDL, the fixed-end (support) moment = WL/12.

q: 45. The maximum bending moment caused by a large number of equally spaced identical loads on a simply supported beam is (W=wL)
explain: As the number of equal point loads increases, the loading approaches a UDL, so max BM approaches WL/8.

q: 46. The maximum bending moment caused by a moment M applied at a distance 'a' from one end on a simply supported beam is (where L=span, a>L/2)
explain: As per the answer key for this specific case (a > L/2).

q: 47. For a beam of uniform strength if its depth is maintained constant then its width will vary in proportion to
explain: As per the answer key for this set (uniform-strength beam with constant depth).

q: 48. In a simply supported beam with span (L) having a triangular load with its intensity 0 at both ends and W at center. The maximum BM will be
explain: As per the answer key for this symmetric triangular loading case.

q: 49. Maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to concentrated load (w) at the mid point is
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/48EI for a central point load on a simply supported beam.

q: 50. In a simply supported beam with span L subjected to a point load W at center, find the maximum bending moment induced in the beam
explain: M_max = WL/4 for a central point load on a simply supported beam.
